sources.incomplete_combustion: FIRE-005: below an O2 fraction of 0.18 part of the carbon forms CO. Burning to CO saves the 1/2 mol of O2 and the 283 kJ that CO's own combustion would take and give (FIRE-003), so 802 - 283 = 519 kJ/mol
sources.enthalpy: FIRE-003: 802 kJ/mol, the heat of combustion with the water as vapour. From standard enthalpies of formation at 298.15 K, CO2(g) -393.522 plus 2 x H2O(g) -241.826 less CH4(g) -74.873 kJ/mol gives -802.30 kJ/mol: NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables C-095, H-064 and C-067, https://janaf.nist.gov/
sources.flammability: FIRE-003: flammability limits in air 5-15 %, autoignition 810 K
